question:
Choose the idiom / phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

People were **very angry** over the demolition of the old theatre.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Up in arms"** means being very angry or upset about something. (गुस्से में या नाराज़ होना)

 
 
• **Example: **The community was **up in arms** over the proposed construction of a new highway through their neighborhood.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Break a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ देना): To wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.

 
 
• **Example:** Before the play started, everyone told the actors to break a leg.
 
 
 
• **Run out of steam** (ऊर्जा या उत्साह खोना): To lose energy or enthusiasm for something.
 
 
• **Example:** He started the project with a lot of excitement, but he ran out of steam halfway through.
 
 
 
• **Armchair critic** (अकारण आलोचना करने वाला): Someone who offers opinions on something without actually being involved or having direct experience.
 
 
• **Example:** He's such an armchair critic; he always has something to say about the team's performance, but he's never played a single match himself.
